en: When leaf stomata open to absorb carbon dioxide for photosynthesis, water vapor simultaneously escapes from the plant into the air.
When a Venus flytrap's sensitive trigger hairs are touched twice within twenty seconds, its leaves rapidly snap shut to trap insects.
The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes that gather maximum light, allowing it to hunt insects effectively in the dark forest at night.
Mangrove trees grow specialized above-ground roots that trap ocean sediment, which builds coastal land and protects shorelines from strong waves.
The pancreas releases the hormone insulin into the bloodstream, which signals body cells to absorb glucose and lower blood sugar levels.
Red blood cells contain hemoglobin, a protein that binds to oxygen in the lungs and transports it to all body tissues.
Inside a chrysalis, a caterpillar's body completely breaks down into a cellular fluid that provides the building blocks to form a butterfly.
As tadpoles undergo metamorphosis, they grow lungs and legs, allowing them to transition from breathing underwater to living on land.
Foraging bees transfer pollen from the male anthers of one flower to the female stigma of another, enabling seed production.
Fungi decompose dead wood by releasing digestive enzymes that break down tough plant matter into nutrient-rich soil for new growth.
A carabao lacks sweat glands, so it wallows in mud to cool its body temperature and protect its skin from the sun.
Cacti evolved sharp spines instead of broad leaves to minimize water evaporation and protect themselves from thirsty desert herbivores.
